FRONTIER RESEARCH ROUND — 8 OCTOBER 2026
Current status: substantial scoped mathematical progress; no established major breakthrough.

The highest-upside lead is a single-manifold extension of the release's three-dimensional
harmonic-dimension construction; its final source-audit status is recorded in Section 5.
The strongest self-contained outcomes are a constructive full-state trace-distance
approximation in a collective quantum thermal model, an exact stochastic recurrence
classification, and a counterexample plus repair for an external detyping lemma.
Historical novelty and external specialist correctness remain unestablished.

1. COLLECTIVE THERMAL STATES: AN EXPLICIT SEPARABLE APPROXIMATION

Model: N qubits initially I/2^N, ideal collective generator
(nu_N+1)D[J_-]+nu_N D[J_+], unnormalized J_a=sum_i sigma_a/2, and its selected
sector-preserving stationary state rho_N. Suppose nu_N/sqrt(N) -> c>0.
Let d_N=inf_{sigma fully separable} ||rho_N-sigma||_1/2.

New upper construction:
  limsup_N d_N <= delta(c)
    <= min{1,2(2/3)^(3/2) exp[-pi^2 c^2+1/(12c^2)]},
  delta(c) ~ 2(2/3)^(3/2) exp[-pi^2 c^2] as c -> infinity AFTER N -> infinity.
The proof gives an explicit positive finite-N mixture of nonidentical pure product
qubits. An exact Euler/Laplace decomposition reduces the problem to mean-field Gibbs
components; two independent proofs establish full trace-norm convergence through
normalized tracial L2. Weak convergence of collective observables alone was not used
as a substitute for the full-state assertion.

At c=1 the integral bound is approximately 5.81897e-5 by numerical quadrature; the
closed analytic bound is approximately 6.12026e-5. The inherited distance-to-identity
comparator is about 0.18963665. These are asymptotic bounds, not finite-N error certificates.

Independently obtained lower bound, using a bounded effect uniform over all fullSEP:
  liminf_N d_N >= [1-sqrt(3/2-2m(c)^2)]^2 >0 when m(c)>1/2,
where m(c)=integral_0^infinity 8sqrt(2/pi)r^2 exp(-2r^2)[r coth(r/c)-c]dr.
The witness endpoint is defined by m(c_w)=1/2 (numerically c_w≈0.3281137031).
The endpoint itself and the polynomial occupation exponent1/2 were inherited; the
bounded-effect trace-distance strengthening and positive approximation are new deductions
of this run. The two bounds do not meet. Exact limiting distance, positivity above c_w,
and an intrinsic separability threshold
